newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen softer before nuke restarts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen softer before nuke restarts.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open lower Tuesday ahead of the two units at the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) returning to operation this week.
Asked about the reason behind the market's early softness, a West Coast broker said, "It's the expectation that the San Onofre units coming back."

In over-the-counter trading, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted $35.40-35.55 a megawatt hour (MWh) down from Monday's settlement at $35.54. August California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $22.20-22.35 a MWh down from yesterday's close at $22.53.
Southern California Edison said the 1,070 megawatt (MW) SONGS unit 2 in San Clemente, Calif., was scheduled to reconnect to the grid this afternoon after a repair outage.
The neighboring 1,080 MW SONGS unit 3 was set to resume operation Thursday after being shut since April for refueling, maintenance and repairs.
Despite rising temperatures in the Southwest, players expect the two SONGS would offset the incremental increase in air-conditioning demand, market sources said.

The Pacific Northwest was expected to see readings rising to one to five degrees Fahrenheit above normal with a chance of showers midweek, while the Southwest would continue to experience dry and seasonal hot weather.
Strength in daily power prices and natural gas futures are expected to cushion a drop in electricity futures, traders and brokers said.
Day-ahead firm, peak prices at PV were quoted at $40.50-41.00 a MWh and those at COB $17.00-18.25.
As of 1010 EDT, NYMEX August Henry Hub gas futures were at 3.4 cents at $21.85 per million British thermal units.
In addition to the SONGS units, the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state continued to increase production. Its output reached 56 percent early Tuesday.
The 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming was said to startup Wednesday.
